newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Arcadia says Dublin Hill results strong.
newsitem.headline: Arcadia says Dublin Hill results strong.

text.p: Gold explorer Arcadia Minerals Ltd on Sunday released new drilling results from the Mount Olympus gold prospect in Western Australia which it said were very encouraging.
The Mount Olympus lode, which is owned by the Dublin Hill joint venture, was up to 150 metres wide and had been extended for an additional 300 metres from the crest of Mt Olympus, Arcadia said.
The lode was still open along strike and 200 metres below the surface, it said.

The Dublin Hill joint venture is 30 percent owned by Arcadia and 70 percent owned by Sipa Resources International NL, which is currently offering five Sipa shares for every three Arcadia shares in a takeover bid.
"The latest 13 reverse circulation holes and two diamond drill holes included a 22 metre intersection that averaged 10.2 grams per tonne (g/t) from a a depth of 203 metres," Arcadia said.
"This included one metre bonanza grades of 105 g/t, 103 g/t, 94 g/t, 84 g/t and 47 g/t, which were cut at 30 g/t to arrive at the 10 g/t average," it said.
"These results are very encouraging for the joint venture partners as the Olympus lode has now been extended," Arcadia Chairman Peter Ho said in a statement.
Arcadia said it had set aside A$2 million for the current drilling programme.
Arcadia has told shareholders not to accept Sipa's takeover bid while Arcadia prepares a formal Part B response.
"We urge our shareholders not to accept the offer until we have fully evaluated it -- at this stage we consider the offer as too low," Ho said.
Arcadia's share price closed up four cents at 79 cents on Friday, while Sipa's price closed down one cent at 48 cents.
